# Atthavasapakaraṇa (Pvr 9)

**ID:** Pvr 9  
**Section:** Parivāra (pvr)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Atthavasapakaraṇa  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m4.mul5.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m4.mul5.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Atthavasapakaraṇa* ("Exposition of Reasons") is a concise treatise belonging to the *Parivāra*, the final collection of the Vinaya Piṭaka [Horner, Book of the Discipline VI]. Its primary subject is an explanation of the ten reasons or purposes (*atthavasa*) for which training rules were laid down by the Buddha for his disciples: the excellence of the Saṅgha, the comfort of the Saṅgha, the restraint of evil-minded individuals, the living in comfort of well-behaved monastics, and the restraint of present and future defilements or cankers (*āsava*) [Horner, Book of the Discipline VI]. In modern digital editions it is numbered as Pvr 9, but in the structure analyzed by I. B. Horner, it constitutes the second division of Chapter VII, concluding with the explicit colophon *Atthavasapakaraṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ* before the end of the *Parivāra*'s *Mahāvagga* section [Horner, Book of the Discipline VI; Horner, Parivara]. Horner observes that counting this text and its preceding division (*Uposathādivissajjanā*) as separate chapters helps arrive at the traditional count of sixteen *parivāras* recorded in the commentaries [Horner, Parivara].

 The text was translated into English by I. B. Horner and by Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner, Book of the Discipline VI].

**Parallels and text reuse**
